problem: Which of the following expressions gives all of the zeros of the function $f(x)=2\operatorname{cot}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{3})?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.

feedback.problem: What is the domain of the function $f(x)=2\operatorname{cot}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{4})+1?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.
feedback.worked_solution:
The domain of $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡x$ is given by

$$
x\ne n\pi ,
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

To find the domain of $2\operatorname{cot}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{4})+1,$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $(x-\frac{\pi }{4}).$ This gives

$$
x-\frac{\pi }{4}\ne n\pi .
$$

Solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x-\frac{\pi }{4} & \ne n\pi  \\ x & \ne n\pi +\frac{\pi }{4} \\ x & \ne \frac{\pi }{4}+n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the domain of the function is $x\ne \frac{\pi }{4}+n\pi ,$ where $n$ is an integer.
